title: Suphan Buri–Nakhon Pathom 2-Day Trip: Temples & Floating Markets | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night road trip linking Suphan Buri and Nakhon Pathom in Thailand: Phra Pathom Chedi, Luang Pho To at Wat Pa Lelai, Don Wai floating market and the century-old Sam Chuk market, with real opening hours and a no-backtrack driving route.
keywords: Suphan Buri Nakhon Pathom trip, 2-province itinerary Thailand, Phra Pathom Chedi, Don Wai floating market, Sam Chuk market
h1:
Suphan Buri–Nakhon Pathom
Temples & Floating Markets, 2 Days 1 Night
intro: These two provinces sit right next to each other — about an hour or so by car — so it's easy to pair them on one trip. The combination that works best is big temples and floating markets: pay your respects to the giant Buddha in the morning, then stroll a riverside market and eat well in the afternoon, before drifting north to spend the night in Suphan Buri. The next day you walk a century-old market. We've laid the route out as a one-way loop with no backtracking, plus real opening hours and good places to stop and eat along the way.
chips: 🛶 Markets on the Tha Chin River

blocks.html: Suphan Buri and Nakhon Pathom make a great pair because they sit on opposite sides of the same Tha Chin River. Driving from downtown Nakhon Pathom up to downtown Suphan Buri takes about an hour and a half, passing through Kamphaeng Saen district. The route is straight and uncomplicated, ideal for Bangkok folks who want a quick escape without going far — temples, markets and local food all in one trip.

This plan starts in Nakhon Pathom because it's closer to Bangkok, then works its way north to finish in Suphan Buri. Leaving early on the first day means you reach the big temple before the crowds build up. We've written the times around when each place actually opens, with driving and parking already factored in.

items: Day 1 (Nakhon Pathom): Phra Pathom Chedi → Sanam Chandra Palace → Don Wai floating market → drive up to Suphan Buri and check in
Day 2 (Suphan Buri): Wat Pa Lelai to pay respects to Luang Pho To → Dragon Descendants Park → century-old Sam Chuk market → head home
Total distance: roughly 180–200 km for the whole trip — relaxed driving, nothing tiring
Good for: families, temple-goers, food lovers, and anyone who wants a close-by trip with no flights and no days off work

blocks.title: Driving is by far the easiest way
blocks.html: Both provinces are easiest to explore with your own car, since the sights are spread out and the floating markets sit outside town. Without a car, you can take a Bangkok–Nakhon Pathom or Bangkok–Suphan Buri van and then grab local transport in town, but you'll spend a lot more time waiting around.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Nakhon Pathom: the giant Buddha and Don Wai floating market

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Nakhon Pathom: the giant Buddha, the palace gardens, the floating market

items.activity: Leave Bangkok and head for Nakhon Pathom
items.note: About 55 km, a bit over an hour's drive if traffic's clear. You can stop for breakfast along the way.

items.activity: Phra Pathom Chedi (Wat Phra Pathom Chedi Ratchaworamahawihan)
items.note: The tallest golden stupa in Thailand, open 07:00–20:00. Pay your respects to Phra Ruang Rochanarit in the northern hall and take a lap around the chedi while the morning sun is still gentle.
King Rama VI's palace, with Thai-European buildings set in shady gardens. Open 09:00–16:00, closed on public holidays. Pleasant for photos around the throne halls and grounds.

items.activity: Lunch break in Nakhon Pathom town
items.note: Try the well-known red pork and crispy pork over rice near the chedi, or beef noodles. The night market opposite the chedi has plenty to eat if you come in the evening.

items.activity: Don Wai floating market, Sam Phran district
items.note: An old market on the Tha Chin River in front of Wat Khongkharam, open daily 08:00–17:00. Packed with food — five-spice braised duck, ho mok, Thai sweets — and you can sit and eat by the water. Weekdays are quieter than weekends.

items.activity: Drive up to Suphan Buri town
items.note: Through Kamphaeng Saen district, about an hour and a half. Check in to your place in Suphan Buri and rest up.
Suphan Buri is known for boat noodles and fish noodles. Shops in town stay open into the evening — after dinner, take a stroll around town before heading back to your room.

blocks.title: A note on Don Wai floating market
blocks.html: For the liveliest atmosphere, come on a weekend, but if you'd rather skip the crush, weekdays are easier to walk and most shops are still open. Parking is available both at the temple and at private lots around the market.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Suphan Buri: Luang Pho To and the century-old market

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Suphan Buri: Luang Pho To, the dragon park, Sam Chuk market

items.activity: Wat Pa Lelai Worawihan, to pay respects to Luang Pho To
items.note: A huge seated Buddha in the Pa Lelai posture at the center of the hall — the city's revered Buddha image. Khum Khun Phaen is nearby if you want to walk on. Opens early, so visit before the sun gets harsh.

items.activity: Dragon Descendants Park / Dragon Descendants Museum
items.note: A giant dragon-shaped building; inside, you walk through rooms tracing Chinese history. There's an entrance fee. Kids love it, and the dragon outside makes for great photos.

items.activity: Lunch before heading to Sam Chuk
items.note: There are several roadside restaurants on the way to Sam Chuk district, or hold out and eat at Sam Chuk market itself — there's far more to choose from there.

items.activity: Century-old Sam Chuk market, Sam Chuk district
items.note: An old wooden market on the Tha Chin River, over a hundred years old, open 08:00–17:00. Walk around for old-style coffee, noodles and Thai sweets, and stop by the Khun Chamnong Chinarak House, a small museum inside the market.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs and pack up to head home
items.note: Suphan Buri souvenirs include Asian pears, local sweets and dried fish. Leaving Sam Chuk in the late afternoon gets you back to Bangkok before the evening traffic.

blocks.html: If you've got the energy and can start early, you could swap in or add Bueng Chawak Chaloem Phra Kiat on Day 2. It's a nature learning center with an aquarium and a zoo, the entry fee is reasonable, and it suits families with kids — but it adds another half-day and sits a fair way from town.

blocks.text: Tweak the plan to your style

items.name: Families with kids
items.blurb: Add Bueng Chawak on Day 2 — it has an aquarium and a zoo, enough to keep kids busy all afternoon, so trim a little of the market time.

items.name: All-temple route
items.blurb: Add Wat Phai Rong Wua, with its many Buddha images and sculptures, after Luang Pho To, for a full day of merit-making.

items.name: Food first
items.blurb: Give Don Wai and Sam Chuk markets all the time they deserve — drop the palace and the dragon park, and just eat your way through.

blocks.text: Things to know before you go

items: Dress modestly — Phra Pathom Chedi and Wat Pa Lelai are important temples, so skip spaghetti straps and shorts above the knee, and take off your shoes before entering the halls.
Carry cash — many stalls at the floating market and the century-old market take cash only, so keep small notes handy for food.
Avoid the midday heat — walking around the chedi and shooting photos in the open palace grounds gets very hot at noon, so it's more comfortable in the morning or late afternoon.
Allow extra time for traffic on the way back — Sunday evenings are busy heading into Bangkok, so leaving Suphan Buri before mid-afternoon makes for a smoother drive.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive between Suphan Buri and Nakhon Pathom?
faq.a: About an hour and a half from downtown Nakhon Pathom to downtown Suphan Buri, passing through Kamphaeng Saen district. The route is straight and uncomplicated, so it's easy to pair the two into a 2-day, 1-night trip without backtracking.

faq.q: Which province should I stay overnight in for this trip?
faq.a: We'd suggest one night in Suphan Buri town, since the plan runs north from Nakhon Pathom and finishes in Suphan Buri. Waking up there on Day 2, you can visit Luang Pho To and walk Sam Chuk market without rushing.

faq.q: Can I do this trip without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's not as convenient, since the floating markets and several sights sit outside town. You can take Bangkok–Nakhon Pathom and Bangkok–Suphan Buri vans and then grab local transport, but you'll spend more time waiting and be more limited on where you can go than with your own car.

faq.q: What days are Don Wai and Sam Chuk markets open?
faq.a: Don Wai floating market (Nakhon Pathom) and the century-old Sam Chuk market (Suphan Buri) are open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00. Weekends are busier and livelier, while weekdays are easier to walk and most shops are still open.

faq.q: What time does Phra Pathom Chedi open?
faq.a: Wat Phra Pathom Chedi opens roughly 07:00–20:00. We'd recommend going in the morning before the sun gets harsh and the crowds arrive, so you can take a lap around the chedi and pay your respects to Phra Ruang Rochanarit in comfort.
